key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly improve oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, with enhanced structural stability versus LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a materials-design route for oxide electrocatalysts in water electrolysis, rather than AI or solar-cell technology.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Connect structural defects and Ni valence with spectroscopy and OER measurements.
Use first-principles calculations to interpret rare-earth–oxygen–nickel electronic hybridization.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films show earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and scalability beyond epitaxial thin films remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
